Carlos — thanks again for the call this morning. A quick follow-up to capture the asks we discussed and to confirm what evidence you need from us to close the DPA/TIA conversation for the APAC pilot.

High level questions from your team we noted:
- Which transfer mechanisms apply to AnzHealth data paths (SCCs / TIA / DTIA / local onshore fallback)?
- Do we need to include the UK IDTA / UK addendum in the DPA for any subset of the pilot (you mentioned a UK analytics center)?
- Subprocessor list and whether proxying/onshore cache is acceptable as an alternative to full residency.

Attached is a short DPA draft with our current subprocessor roster and a preliminary TIA scoping checklist — both are to give you a starting point. Can you confirm which of the transfer mechanisms above your legal team requires, and whether we should prepare: (a) a full TIA evidence pack (logs + KV cache attestations + keystore topology), or (b) a limited DTIA summary for processors only?

Next steps we propose from Redwood:
1) Kimberly will confirm the technical mapping (transit nodes, onshore cache fallback patterns) and list the artifacts we can provide within 3 business days.
2) Jonas will prepare a short note on our fallback routing policies and automatic model-variant fallback that might affect residency.
3) Laura to coordinate a targeted legal-to-legal call if AnzHealth needs UK addendum commitment.

Appreciate a narrow list of must-have artifacts so we can prioritize.

Thanks,

Laura — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Helpful. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing with Legal: 

1) Primary ask: we need to understand whether any customer data for the pilot will transit through EU/UK regions. If so, we need SCCs and the UK addendum paperwork for that subset. If processing is strictly APAC-resident, we still require a TIA/DTIA summary showing safeguards for cross-border telemetry and backups.

2) Subprocessors: provide the current roster plus a short description of roles (e.g., logging/monitoring, inference runtime, caching). We will triage which subprocessors require additional attestation.

3) Evidence level: our preference is to start with a DTIA summary for initial procurement (we want to avoid heavy lift right before pilot go-live), but Legal has reserved the right to request the full TIA evidence pack within 30 days if any EU/UK transit is detected.

Could Kimberly confirm the transit topology and whether automatic fallback could route tokens to an EU fallback region for latency reasons? That specific behavior will drive whether we need SCCs/UK addendum.

Carlos

Carlos — quick technical summary below. I'll attach the short topology diagram to the shared Drive link after this thread.

Key points:
- Default routing: customer requests anchored to the region of the model endpoint. For your APAC pilot we'll use ap-southeast-1 endpoints unless you opt for multi-region. That means inference compute and model KV caches are in APAC by default.
- Edge/transit: telemetry (metrics/traces) and certain orchestration heartbeats are sent to our global control plane, which currently has endpoints in NA/EU/APAC. Telemetry contains no user prompt text; operational logs are pseudonymized.
- Automatic fallback: only triggered on capacity constraints for the pinned APAC pool. Fallback hierarchy: APAC burst -> Dedicated shared APAC -> cross-region fallback (primarily US), EU used only as a last-resort for specific reserved models. Fallback to EU is rare but possible.
- Onshore cache fallback: we can enable an onshore-response-cache (APAC-only) to avoid cross-region model calls for repeat prefixes; that is an opt-in configuration.

Artifacts we can provide immediately:
- current subprocessor roster (roles + hosting region)
- topology diagram + control-plane telemetry pseudonymization statement
- onshore cache config guide and verification steps

If AnzHealth wants to avoid any EU/UK transit, action required: enforce model pinning to APAC-only and enable onshore cache for critical routes. We can provide a written attestation and a runbook. If Legal insists on proactive SCCs/UK addendum, we can produce the redline DPA and coordinate DocuSign.

I'll upload the diagram and a short DTIA summary to the Drive link and flag any subprocessors that have EU-based operators. Expect that in ~24 hours.

—Kimberly
